chunks: He was asked about a stray sheep in the wilderness, so he said to the questioner: “It is for you, or for your brother, or for the wolf.”

He said: “And I do not like to touch it.” And regarding the stray camel also, he said: “What do you have to do with it? Its belly is its container, its hoof is its shoe, and its stomach is its water carrier. Leave it alone.”

key_terms.الذِّئْبِ: the wolf; indicating the danger facing an unattended sheep
key_terms.الشَّاةِ: a sheep; here, a stray sheep found in the open land
key_terms.الْفَلَاةِ: the wilderness or open desert land
key_terms.سِقَاؤُهُ: its water carrier; meaning it can endure and manage on its own
key_terms.وِعَاؤُهُ: its container; meaning it carries its own means of sustenance

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on finding a stray sheep or camel in the wilderness?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on stray animals found in the wilderness. A stray sheep may be taken because it is vulnerable to loss or predation, whereas a stray camel should be left alone because it can protect and sustain itself until its owner finds it.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.4057 - Imam (as) was asked about a lost sheep in the wilderness.
Imam (as) said to the questioner: "It is either yours, your brother's, or the wolf's."

Then Imam (as) said: "I do not like to touch it."
And when asked about a lost camel, Imam (as) said: "What do you have to do with it? Its belly is its container, its hooves are its shoes, and its stomach is its water carrier. Leave it alone."
